newsitem.title: CHILE: Banco Santiago holders approve merger.
newsitem.headline: Banco Santiago holders approve merger.

text.p: Chile's Banco de Santiago said shareholders on Thursday approved plans to merge with Banco O'Higgins and gave the go-ahead to plans to repay Banco de Santiago debt owed to the Central Bank.
The $1.8 billion of debt, incurred in a financial crisis in the early 1980s, will be repaid by giving a shareholding in the merged bank to the Central Bank, it said.
The Central Bank will receive newly created E series shares in the merged bank, which will be called Banco Santiago, said bank officials at a special shareholder meeting.
Under the debt repayment agreement, agreed to in October after months of negotiations, the Central Bank will own 38.54 percent of the merged bank.

Officials said the Central Bank had fixed a price of 12.54 pesos for its E-series shares, which will offered to existing shareholders in coming months. Those shares not sold will be offered to the public in the second half of 1997.
Santiago and O'Higgins are both controlled by the Luksic industrial group. The merged bank will be among Chile's largest private banks.
O'Higgins stockholders are to vote on the deal at a meeting at 1600 local/1900 GMT Thursday.
